feature: how a Rushes video is put together

opening.title: Two registers, one video
opening.subtitle: Designed slides explain; the live app proves
opening.disclaimer: A bundled fixture application. No real data appears in this video.
opening.narration: A Rushes video alternates two things: designed slides that explain a concept, and the real application filmed live.

scenes.narration: The pipeline has five stages. A storyboard becomes narration, the narration sets the clock, the browser is driven against the real app, the finished file is measured, and only then is anything delivered.
The check is the part that is different. Three tiers of evidence, and they are never conflated: deterministic checks, automated frame evidence, and a human who actually watched it.
And this is the other register: the same video cuts to the real application, where the claim on the slide has to survive contact with the running software.

closing.title: Point it at your app
closing.subtitle: rushes init, then describe the demo
closing.narration: Point it at your own application, describe the demo you want, and let the checker decide whether it is fit to publish.
